topic: Privacy-First Contact Tracing: The DP-3T Algorithm
target_audience: University students in Computer Science or Data Privacy

sections.title: The Privacy-Security Paradox
lecture_lines: Traditional contact tracing often relies on central surveillance.
This risks exposing sensitive user location and identity.
DP-3T provides a decentralized, privacy-first alternative approach.
animations: Create a central white server icon (#FFFFFF) connected to grey phone icons [Asset: /mmfs1/data/group/pmc082/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/phone.svg] (#AAAAAA) by thin red lines.

sections.title: Generating Digital Disguises (Ephemeral IDs)
lecture_lines: Each phone generates a daily Secret Key (SK).
A cryptographic hash function transforms this Secret Key.
This creates thousands of temporary Ephemeral IDs.
IDs rotate every fifteen minutes to prevent tracking.
To others, the user appears as a new person.

sections.title: The Invisible Handshake (BLE Exchange)
lecture_lines: Nearby phones detect each other using Bluetooth signals.
This local exchange occurs directly between the devices.
Crucially, no central server tracks this interaction.
Each phone records these encounters in a local diary.
Received IDs are stored securely on the user's device.

Show a central white server icon (#FFFFFF) with a large red 'X' (#FF0000) while 'EphID' labels move between the phones.

sections.title: The Diagnosis Report (Infection Event)
lecture_lines: Infected users voluntarily share their daily Secret Keys.
No personal names or locations are ever uploaded.
These keys are published on a public bulletin board.

sections.title: Local Matching: The Final Privacy Shield
lecture_lines: Phones periodically download the list of infected keys.
Each phone locally regenerates the corresponding Ephemeral IDs.
It checks for matches within its own seen diary.
Matching occurs privately without notifying the central server.
Users get alerts while maintaining total digital anonymity.
